title: A working environment before implementation and verification
legacy_excerpt: Before dispatching implementation agents, confirm the infrastructure the feature needs, such as the dev servers, is still running.
finding: Isolation and final checks remain, but there is no practical readiness step for configuration keys, services, migrations, seed data, or a running app.
restore: Add a shared environment-readiness reference used by feature and Whetstone routes. Read project setup instructions, identify prerequisites without exposing secret values, start the real app, and verify the intended environment. Keep unavailable prerequisites visible as blockers.
history: Already absent in this detail from the pre-runbook public package.

title: Concrete verification after landing
legacy_excerpt:
- [ ] **Error monitoring:** No new errors in logs, error tracking, or monitoring dashboards
- [ ] **Performance:** No significant degradation in response times or resource usage
finding: The new text says to verify the release and distinguish merged, deployed, and enabled. It no longer supplies the operational checks that make that statement useful.
restore: Automate post-launch verification as far as possible. Use repeatable scripts for operational checks and Playwright against the live site. Have an LLM examine the deployed feature or bug-fix flow using actual browser interaction and captured evidence. Record the deployed revision, health, applicable migrations, error monitoring, performance, flag state, recovery, script output, browser evidence, and LLM findings. Missing required checks leave verification incomplete and require follow-through. Do not restore a routine human checklist or approval gate.
history: The detailed checklist was not in the pre-runbook public package.

title: A stable progress page with meaningful update events
legacy_excerpt: The lede is rewritten on every update
finding: Progress is reduced to a list of topics. The creation/opening step, accountable writer, task owners, current blockers, and event-driven updates are no longer explained.
restore: Provide a compact progress template with current state, attention needed, active owners, document links, acceptance/evidence, decisions, and next action. Update it when work starts or ends, a review returns, a blocker changes, or a release lands. Use actual tool timestamps. Do not freeze the old phase numbers or exact heading count.
history: The public template was already compressed before the runbook rewrite.

title: Separate worker detail and durable review history

outcome, changed files, verification commands and evidence paths, a quick screenshot when the work has a visible surface, deviations,
blockers, follow-ups, and `## Cleanup needed`.

restore: Add an optional worker-return template and review-round template. Name one writer per detail file, link evidence, preserve earlier review rounds, and keep decisions in the owning source. This helps unattended work resume without reconstructing the conversation.

title: Document authoring and source-to-render instructions

Use the existing includes and review-sibling composition. Edit source files and rebuild the human document to keep both views in sync. Add a focused authoring reference linking the installed review tool's component catalog and explaining source versus generated output. Keep simple direct Markdown review available. Preserve historical conventions instead of rewriting documents to fit a tool.

title: An explicit bar for the finished user experience
legacy_excerpt: Honest feedback. Toasts and status messages report what actually happened. Never an optimistic "done" for something still in flight, or something that failed.
finding: The new route retains high-fidelity prototypes, staff design, customer personas, and design-language references. The concrete acceptance floor for the integrated product is weaker.
restore: Use the reviewed prototype or styles and user feedback as the design acceptance baseline. Verify implementation fidelity and fix drift; do not let later reviewers replace approved aesthetics with their preferences. Surface material new issues or conflicts rather than silently redesigning. When no reviewed baseline exists, have the agent perform its own proportional design review of hierarchy, components/tokens, responsive and accessible states, honest feedback, motion, voice, and coherence. Functional, accessibility, and required verification checks still apply to approved designs. Encode repeatable project style rules in existing linters or equivalent checks: token bypasses, prohibited inline styles, token-documentation drift, and reliably detectable component-use rules. Respect project policy and narrow legitimate exceptions. Run checks through normal verification, with hooks where useful, and test them against violating and valid fixtures. Do not require another reviewer roster.
history: The richer Plan acceptance criteria were already absent from the public baseline.

decision_note: Excluded from the restoration plan by the user. Preserve the historical comparison; do not implement this proposed restoration.
title: Operational code-review prompts, especially the cost of writes
legacy_excerpt:
- How often does it write? Per keystroke, per event, per poll, per commit? Name the trigger.
- How much does each write carry? The changed part, or the whole record or file?
finding: Reviewer ownership and findings improved. Specific checks for write amplification, API compatibility, queries, idempotence, actionable errors, privacy, and operational logging are now mostly left to generic judgment or selected principles.
restore: Add risk-triggered reviewer prompts. Preserve the unusual write-frequency/payload/flush check. Include a publishing check for secrets and sensitive data. Reuse existing pstack leaves rather than copying overlapping general advice.
history: The concrete checklist did not exist in the pre-runbook public package.

title: A complete closeout, including small changes
legacy_excerpt: Lessons are written as they happen
finding: Docs, diagrams, lessons, and owned cleanup remain in the new text. The explicit obligation to check them even for small changes, capture each surprise, and close the whole record has softened.
restore: Add a portable closeout reference: verify commits/push and release, check durable docs/diagrams, record surprises as lessons, place follow-ups on the existing board, close progress, and inspect owned worktrees before teardown. Preserve the distinction between a lesson and a bug ticket. Avoid mandatory private skills or a long ceremony.
history: The detailed lifecycle was absent earlier. The small-change lesson requirement was softened specifically by the runbook rewrite; compare the earlier public Whetstone cleanup change.

title: A compact document consistency and feasibility check
legacy_excerpt: - [ ] The plan covers every component described in the architecture. No architecture component is orphaned.
finding: Requirements, alternatives, contracts, and the Plan table remain. The explicit check that the documents describe the same scope and a feasible integrated build is no longer concrete.
restore: Offer a short author self-check for scope/terminology agreement, chosen rather than rejected alternatives, unresolved assumptions, orphaned components, dependencies, and failure coverage. Do not restore the old EM/code-lead chain or confidence cutoff.
history: This is from the older installed Codex copy, not an asserted contract of the recent public package.

title: Product thinking before the prototype
legacy_excerpt: Challenge premise, force alternatives, answer "what if we do nothing,"
finding: The separate installed Crucible skill covered user jobs, evidence, product assumptions, roadmap priority, opportunity cost, and alternatives. The new prototype route only says to resolve the premise. The original audit understated this as a no-build prompt.
restore: Restore lightweight product thinking before the short brief and prototype. Clarify the real user job and context, status quo, evidence, product assumptions, priority against named board alternatives, opportunity cost, and whether to reuse, adopt, reduce scope, build, or do nothing. Record a recommendation, uncertainty, user corrections, and next action in a focused note that feeds the brief and composed document. Keep requirements and architecture out of premises. Scale depth to uncertainty without a rigid interview, compulsory premise voting, forced alternatives, or routine approval gate.
history: The public router summarized premise challenges and doing nothing. The fuller product-thinking workflow lives in the separately inspected installed Crucible source, outside the preserved five-skill snapshot; no particular public Git revision is asserted for it.

title: Helper for preparing agent assignments
finding: The current helper only captures verification runs. The old packet command selected source headings and validated the contract fields; the contract concept itself survives.
restore: The original purpose was to reduce token usage by giving each agent less text. An optional script would assemble an agent's goal, constraints, completion checks, and selected documentation sections into a Markdown assignment, refusing missing required fields. The smaller dossier and selective source reading may already suffice. Recommend deferring the script and inspecting what workers actually receive. Restore it only if observed avoidable context cost remains; clear assignments do not depend on this helper.
history: This command was already absent from the first public helper.
